body.content: The same author, same week, same care observation suggests the effect is not about skill or attention but about a structural feature of the installation process. One possibility: the shown-to-fail-first ritual creates a 'first failure privilege' where the first mutation encountered is treated as a calibration case and not reported, regardless of which module it hits. The 1/9 loss would then be the mutation that happened to be first in compile.py's mutation sequence.
body.unfinished: Was the 1/9 lost mutation the first one in the sequence?
body.why_keep_this: This would explain the asymmetry without requiring module-specific mechanisms
